nodes.name: Minimal polynomial degree bound
nodes.statement: Let $R \to S$ be a finite free extension with $R$ nontrivial. For any $\alpha \in S$, \[ \deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_R \alpha) \le \operatorname{finrank}_R S. \]
assumptions: Let $R \to S$ be a finite free extension with $R$ nontrivial.
$\alpha \in S$
nodes.statement_short: The minimal polynomial of an element of a finite free extension has degree at most the rank.
nodes.label: lem:minpoly_natDegree_le

nodes.name: Proof of the minimal polynomial degree bound
nodes.statement: Let $\ell_\alpha = \operatorname{Algebra.lmul}_R\, \alpha$ be the left-multiplication endomorphism. By Cayley--Hamilton ($\mathtt{LinearMap.aeval\_self\_charpoly}$), $\operatorname{aeval}_\alpha(\operatorname{charpoly}(\ell_\alpha)) = 0$. Since $\operatorname{charpoly}(\ell_\alpha)$ is monic, the minimal polynomial divides it, so $\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_R \alpha) \le \deg(\operatorname{charpoly}(\ell_\alpha)) = \operatorname{finrank}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: Cayley-Hamilton for the multiplication map: minpoly divides the monic charpoly, whose degree is the rank.

nodes.name: Quotient isomorphism without integrally closed hypothesis
nodes.statement: Let $R \to S$ be a finite free extension with $R$ nontrivial, and let $\alpha \in S$ with $R[\alpha] = S$. Then $f = \operatorname{minpoly}_R \alpha$ is monic, and the natural map \[ \varphi \colon R[X]/(f) \longrightarrow S, \qquad X \mapsto \alpha \] is an $R$-algebra isomorphism. In particular, $S$ admits an $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure for $f$.
assumptions: Let $R \to S$ be a finite free extension with $R$ nontrivial,
let $\alpha \in S$ with $R[\alpha] = S$.
conclusions: In particular, $S$ admits an $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure for $f$.
nodes.statement_short: If $\alpha$ generates a finite free extension $S$ of $R$, then $R[X]/(\operatorname{minpoly}\alpha)\cong S$, with no integral closedness assumption.
nodes.label: thm:mkOfAdjoinEqTop

nodes.name: Proof of the quotient isomorphism
nodes.statement: The map $\varphi$ is well-defined since $f(\alpha) = 0$, and surjective since $R[\alpha] = S$. \textbf{Rank equality.} The upper bound $\deg f \le \operatorname{finrank}_R S$ follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:minpoly_natDegree_le}. For the lower bound, consider the surjection $\varphi$. By the quotient rank formula ($\mathtt{finrank\_quotient\_}\allowbreak\mathtt{span\_eq\_natDegree'}$), $\operatorname{finrank}_R(R[X]/(f)) = \deg f$. Since $\varphi$ is surjective, $\operatorname{finrank}_R S \le \operatorname{finrank}_R(R[X]/(f)) = \deg f$. Hence $\deg f = \operatorname{finrank}_R S$. \textbf{Injectivity.} Since both $R[X]/(f)$ and $S$ are free $R$-modules of the same finite rank, and $\varphi$ is surjective, the composite $e^{-1} \circ \varphi$ is a surjective endomorphism of a finitely generated free module (where $e$ is a linear equivalence from the rank equality). By $\mathtt{OrzechProperty.}\allowbreak\mathtt{injective\_of\_surjective\_endomorphism}$ (which holds for all commutative rings), this composite is injective, hence $\varphi$ is injective.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\deg f = \operatorname{finrank}_R S$ by two inequalities, then a surjective endomorphism of a free module is injective (Orzech property).

nodes.name: Generator descends to residue fields
nodes.statement: If $\beta$ generates $S$ over $R$ (i.e., $R[\beta] = S$), then $\bar\beta = \beta \bmod \mathfrak{m}_S$ generates $k_S$ over $k_R$.
assumptions: $\beta$ generates $S$ over $R$ (i.e., $R[\beta] = S$)
nodes.label: lem:adjoin_residue_eq_top

nodes.name: Proof that the generator descends
nodes.statement: Given $x \in k_S$, lift to $s \in S$, express $s = p(\beta)$ for some $p \in R[X]$, then $x = \bar{p}(\bar\beta)$ where $\bar{p} = p \bmod \mathfrak{m}_R \in k_R[X]$. The key commutativity ($\operatorname{residue}_S \circ \varphi = \operatorname{algebraMap}_{k_R \to k_S} \circ \operatorname{residue}_R$) is used via $\mathtt{map\_aeval\_eq\_aeval\_map}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lift a residue element, write it as a polynomial in $\beta$, reduce the coefficients.

nodes.name: Rank preserved by residue field base change
nodes.statement: If $R \to S$ is a finite étale extension of local rings with faithful scalar action, then \[ \operatorname{finrank}_R S = \operatorname{finrank}_{k_R} k_S. \]
assumptions: $R \to S$ is a finite étale extension of local rings with faithful scalar action
nodes.label: lem:finrank_eq_finrank_residueField

nodes.name: Proof of rank equality across residue fields
nodes.statement: Since $R \to S$ is étale, it is smooth, hence flat. Finite + flat over a local ring implies free ($\mathtt{Module.free\_of\_flat\_of\_isLocalRing}$). The étale condition gives $\mathfrak{m}_R \cdot S = \mathfrak{m}_S$ ($\mathtt{Algebra.FormallyUnramified.}\allowbreak\mathtt{map\_maximalIdeal}$), so $S / \mathfrak{m}_R S \cong k_S$. By $\mathtt{IsLocalRing.finrank\_quotient\_map}$, $\operatorname{finrank}_{k_R}(S/\mathfrak{m}_R S) = \operatorname{finrank}_R S$. The quotient equivalence from $\mathfrak{m}_R S = \mathfrak{m}_S$ transfers the finrank.
nodes.statement_short: Étale implies flat, hence free; unramifiedness gives $\mathfrak{m}_R S=\mathfrak{m}_S$, and the rank passes to $S/\mathfrak{m}_R S\cong k_S$.

nodes.name: Minimal polynomial maps to residue minimal polynomial
nodes.statement: Let $R \to S$ be a finite étale extension of local rings with faithful scalar action, and $\beta \in S$ with $R[\beta] = S$. Then \[ (\operatorname{minpoly}_R \beta) \bmod \mathfrak{m}_R = \operatorname{minpoly}_{k_R} \bar\beta. \]
nodes.section: 3.3 Minimal Polynomial Descends to Residue Field
assumptions: Let $R \to S$ be a finite étale extension of local rings with faithful scalar action,
$\beta \in S$ with $R[\beta] = S$.
nodes.statement_short: For a generator of a finite étale local extension, reducing its minimal polynomial gives the residue minimal polynomial.
nodes.label: lem:minpoly_map_residue

nodes.name: Proof that the minimal polynomial descends
nodes.statement: Set $f = \operatorname{minpoly}_R \beta$, $\bar f = f \bmod \mathfrak{m}_R$, $g = \operatorname{minpoly}_{k_R} \bar\beta$. Since $\bar\beta$ is a root of $\bar f$ (by $\mathtt{hom\_eval_2}$), we have $g \mid \bar f$. Both $f$ and $g$ are monic, and $\bar f$ is monic. The degree chain: \begin{align*} \deg \bar f &= \deg f && \text{(monic polynomial preserves degree under reduction)} \\ &= \operatorname{finrank}_R S && \text{(Theorem~\ref{thm:mkOfAdjoinEqTop})} \\ &= \operatorname{finrank}_{k_R} k_S && \text{(Lemma~\ref{lem:finrank_eq_finrank_residueField})} \\ &= [k_R(\bar\beta) : k_R] && \text{(Lemma~\ref{lem:adjoin_residue_eq_top}: } k_R[\bar\beta] = k_S \text{)} \\ &= \deg g && \text{(degree of minimal polynomial = extension degree)} \end{align*} Since $g \mid \bar f$, both are monic, and they have the same degree, $\bar f = g$.
nodes.section: 3.3 Minimal Polynomial Descends to Residue Field
nodes.statement_short: Divisibility $g\mid\bar f$ plus equality of degrees of two monic polynomials. The degree chain goes through the quotient isomorphism and the rank equality.

nodes.name: Derivative of minimal polynomial is a unit
nodes.statement: Let $R \to S$ be a finite étale extension of local rings with faithful scalar action, and $\beta \in S$ with $R[\beta] = S$. Then \[ f'(\beta) \in S^\times \] where $f = \operatorname{minpoly}_R \beta$.
assumptions: Let $R \to S$ be a finite étale extension of local rings with faithful scalar action,
$\beta \in S$ with $R[\beta] = S$.
where $f = \operatorname{minpoly}_R \beta$.
nodes.statement_short: For a generator $\beta$ of a finite étale local extension, $f'(\beta)$ is a unit for its minimal polynomial $f$.
nodes.label: thm:isUnit_aeval_derivative_minpoly

nodes.name: Proof of the unit derivative condition
nodes.statement:
Since $S$ is a local ring, it suffices to show $\overline{f'( eta)} 
e 0$ in $k_S$ ($\mathtt{IsLocalRing.}\allowbreak\mathtt{residue\_ne\_zero\_iff\_isUnit}$). Since $R 	o S$ is étale, the residue field extension $k_R 	o k_S$ is separable. By Lemma~ef{lem:minpoly_map_residue}, $ ar f = \operatorname{minpoly}_{k_R}  ar eta$, so $ ar f$ is separable ($\mathtt{Algebra.IsSeparable.isSeparable}$). This means $ ar{f'}( ar eta) 
e 0$ ($\mathtt{Separable.aeval\_derivative\_ne\_zero}$). By $\mathtt{hom\_eval_2}$, $\overline{f'( eta)} =  ar{f'}( ar eta) 
e 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the residue field, where the minimal polynomial is separable since étale gives a separable residue extension.

nodes.name: Finite étale local extensions are monogenic
nodes.statement: Let $R \to S$ be a finite étale extension of local rings with faithful scalar action. Then there exists $\beta \in S$ such that $R[\beta] = S$.
assumptions: Let $R \to S$ be a finite étale extension of local rings with faithful scalar action.
conclusions: there exists $\beta \in S$ such that $R[\beta] = S$.
also_stated_at: A finite injective étale map of local rings is monogenic, and the minimal polynomial has unit derivative.
nodes.label: thm:exists_adjoin_eq_top

nodes.name: Proof of existence of a generator (Nakayama argument)
nodes.statement: By the primitive element theorem ($\mathtt{Field.exists\_primitive\_element}$), there exists $\beta_0 \in k_S$ with $k_R[\beta_0] = k_S$. Lift $\beta_0$ to $\beta \in S$ via $\mathtt{Ideal.Quotient.mk\_surjective}$. It suffices to show $\operatorname{Algebra.adjoin} R \{\beta\} = \top$. By Nakayama's lemma ($\mathtt{Submodule.}\allowbreak\mathtt{le\_of\_le\_smul\_of\_le\_jacobson\_bot}$), it suffices to show $S \subseteq R[\beta] + \mathfrak{m}_R \cdot S$. For any $s \in S$, the residue $\bar s \in k_S = k_R[\beta_0]$, so there exists $t_0 \in R[\beta]$ with $\overline{t_0} = \bar s$. Then $s - t_0 \in \mathfrak{m}_S = \mathfrak{m}_R \cdot S$ (using the étale condition $\mathtt{Algebra.FormallyUnramified.map\_maximalIdeal}$).
nodes.statement_short: Lift a primitive element of the residue extension, then Nakayama's lemma using $\mathfrak{m}_S=\mathfrak{m}_R S$.

nodes.name: Standard étale from monogenic with unit derivative
nodes.statement: Let $f \in R[X]$ be monic with $S \cong R[X]/(f)$ (via an $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure). If $f'(\beta) \in S^\times$ where $\beta$ is the image of $X$, then $R \to S$ is étale.
nodes.section: 4 Converse: Monogenic with Unit Derivative Implies \'Etale
assumptions: Let $f \in R[X]$ be monic with $S \cong R[X]/(f)$ (via an $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure).
$f'(\beta) \in S^\times$ where $\beta$ is the image of $X$,
also_stated_at: A monogenic extension with unit derivative is étale (i.e., standard étale).
nodes.statement_short: A monogenic extension $R[X]/(f)$ with $f'(\beta)$ a unit is (standard) étale.
nodes.label: thm:algebra_etale

nodes.name: Proof that unit derivative gives standard étale
nodes.statement: Construct a $\mathtt{StandardEtalePair}$ using $(f, f')$: the Bézout relation $f' \cdot 1 + f \cdot 0 = (f')^1$ is trivially satisfied. The natural map $P.\mathtt{lift} \colon P.\mathtt{Ring} \to S$ sending $X \mapsto \beta$ is well-defined by $f(\beta) = 0$ and the unit condition on $f'(\beta)$. Construct an explicit inverse via $\mathtt{AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom}$ composed with the algebra equivalence $S \cong \mathtt{AdjoinRoot}\; f$. Verify it is both a left and right inverse by checking on generators, concluding bijectivity. Hence $S$ is standard étale ($\mathtt{Algebra.IsStandardEtale}$), and étale follows.
nodes.section: 4 Converse: Monogenic with Unit Derivative Implies \'Etale
nodes.statement_short: Build a standard étale pair from $(f,f')$ and show its lift to $S$ is bijective via an explicit inverse.

nodes.name: Height-one primes are principal in UFDs
nodes.statement: In a UFD $S$, every prime ideal $\mathfrak{q}$ of height~1 is principal.
assumptions: In a UFD $S$,
prime ideal $\mathfrak{q}$ of height~1
nodes.label: lem:height_one_principal

nodes.name: Proof that height-one primes are principal
nodes.statement: Since $\mathfrak{q} \ne 0$, it contains an irreducible element $p$. Then $\operatorname{span}\{p\}$ is prime and contained in $\mathfrak{q}$. If $\operatorname{span}\{p\} \subsetneq \mathfrak{q}$, then $\operatorname{height}(\operatorname{span}\{p\}) < \operatorname{height}(\mathfrak{q}) = 1$, forcing $\operatorname{span}\{p\} = 0$, contradicting $p \ne 0$. Hence $\mathfrak{q} = \operatorname{span}\{p\}$.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: an irreducible $p\in\mathfrak{q}$ gives a nonzero prime $(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{q}$, which height 1 forces to be all of $\mathfrak{q}$.

nodes.name: Taylor expansion for polynomial evaluation
nodes.statement: For any polynomial $f \in R[X]$ and elements $x, h \in S$, there exists $c \in S$ such that \[ f(x + h) = f(x) + f'(x) \cdot h + h^2 \cdot c. \]
assumptions: For any polynomial $f \in R[X]$ and elements $x, h \in S$,
conclusions: there exists $c \in S$ such that \[ f(x + h) = f(x) + f'(x) \cdot h + h^2 \cdot c. \]
nodes.label: lem:taylor_expansion

nodes.name: Proof of the Taylor expansion
nodes.statement: Reduce modulo $\operatorname{span}\{h^2\}$ using $\mathtt{Polynomial.aeval\_add\_of\_sq\_eq\_zero}$, then lift.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce modulo $(h^2)$ and lift.

nodes.name: Maximal ideal decomposition from étale quotient
nodes.statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be local rings with $S$ a finite $R$-algebra, and let $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ be a prime ideal. If the quotient map $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R) \to S/\mathfrak{q}$ is étale, then \[ \mathfrak{m}_S = \mathfrak{q} + \mathfrak{m}_R \cdot S. \]
assumptions: Let $R$ and $S$ be local rings with $S$ a finite $R$-algebra,
let $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ be a prime ideal.
the quotient map $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R) \to S/\mathfrak{q}$ is étale,
nodes.label: lem:maximalIdeal_eq_sup

nodes.name: Proof of the maximal ideal decomposition
nodes.statement: The quotient rings are local domains, and the étale condition on $R/\mathfrak{p} \to S/\mathfrak{q}$ gives $\mathfrak{m}_{R/\mathfrak{p}} \cdot (S/\mathfrak{q}) = \mathfrak{m}_{S/\mathfrak{q}}$ by $\mathtt{Algebra.FormallyUnramified.map\_maximalIdeal}$. Pulling back through the quotient maps, using $\operatorname{map}(\operatorname{mk}\; \mathfrak{q})(\mathfrak{m}_S) = \mathfrak{m}_{S/\mathfrak{q}}$ and the analogous statement for $R$, the equality lifts to $\mathfrak{m}_S = \mathfrak{q} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: Unramifiedness of the quotient map gives the maximal-ideal equality downstairs; pull it back through the quotient maps.

nodes.name: Quotient adjustment
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ be an ideal and $\mathfrak{q} = \operatorname{span}\{q_0\}$. Then for any $\beta \in S$, the image of $\beta + q_0$ in $S/\mathfrak{q}$ is equal to the image of $\beta$.
assumptions: Let $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ be an ideal and $\mathfrak{q} = \operatorname{span}\{q_0\}$.
for any $\beta \in S$,
conclusions: the image of $\beta + q_0$ in $S/\mathfrak{q}$ is equal to the image of $\beta$.
nodes.label: lem:quotient_adjust

nodes.name: Proof of quotient adjustment
nodes.statement: Since $(\beta + q_0) - \beta = q_0 \in \mathfrak{q}$, the elements are congruent modulo $\mathfrak{q}$.
nodes.statement_short: The difference is $q_0\in\mathfrak{q}$.

nodes.name: Quotient lifting
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ be an ideal and $\beta \in S$. If $\beta$ generates $S/\mathfrak{q}$ over $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R)$, then for every $s \in S$ there exists $t \in R[\beta]$ with $s - t \in \mathfrak{q}$.
assumptions: Let $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ be an ideal and $\beta \in S$.
$\beta$ generates $S/\mathfrak{q}$ over $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R)$,
conclusions: for every $s \in S$ there exists $t \in R[\beta]$ with $s - t \in \mathfrak{q}$.
nodes.label: lem:exists_adjoin_sub_mem

nodes.name: Proof of quotient lifting
nodes.statement: Since $(R/\mathfrak{p})[\bar\beta] = S/\mathfrak{q}$, the map $\operatorname{aeval}_{\bar\beta}$ is surjective. Lift a polynomial preimage of $\bar s$ through $\mathtt{Polynomial.map\_surjective}$ to obtain $t \in R[\beta]$ with $s - t \in \mathfrak{q}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lift a polynomial preimage of $\bar s$ through the surjection on polynomial rings.

nodes.name: Nakayama argument for quotient generation
nodes.statement: Let $R, S$ be local rings with $S$ a finite $R$-algebra, and $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ a prime ideal. Let $\beta \in S$ and $\pi \in R[\beta]$. Assume: \begin{enumerate} \item $\bar\beta$ generates $S/\mathfrak{q}$ over $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R)$, \item $\mathfrak{m}_S = \operatorname{span}\{\pi\} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$. \end{enumerate} Then $R[\beta] = S$.
assumptions: Let $R, S$ be local rings with $S$ a finite $R$-algebra, and $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ a prime ideal.
Let $\beta \in S$ and $\pi \in R[\beta]$.
$\bar\beta$ generates $S/\mathfrak{q}$ over $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R)$,
$\mathfrak{m}_S = \operatorname{span}\{\pi\} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: If $\bar\beta$ generates $S/\mathfrak{q}$ and $\mathfrak{m}_S=(\pi)+\mathfrak{m}_R S$ with $\pi\in R[\beta]$, then $R[\beta]=S$.
nodes.label: lem:adjoin_eq_top_of_quotient

nodes.name: Proof of the Nakayama argument for quotient generation
nodes.statement: Set $A = R[\beta]$. The quotient $S/\mathfrak{m}_R S$ is Artinian (finite over the field $k_R$), so $\mathfrak{m}_S^n \subseteq \mathfrak{m}_R S$ for some $n$. \textbf{Power bound.} By induction, $\mathfrak{m}_S^k \subseteq \operatorname{span}\{\pi^k\} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$, using the hypothesis on $\mathfrak{m}_S$. \textbf{Iterative reduction.} For $x \in \mathfrak{q}$, by repeated application of quotient lifting (Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_adjoin_sub_mem}) and the power bound, we find $a \in A$ with $x - a \in \operatorname{span}\{\pi^n\} + \mathfrak{m}_R S \subseteq \mathfrak{m}_R S$. Hence $\mathfrak{q} \subseteq A + \mathfrak{m}_R S$ as $R$-submodules. Combined with the quotient lifting for general elements, $S \subseteq A + \mathfrak{m}_R S$. By Nakayama's lemma, $A = S$.
nodes.statement_short: Artinian bound $\mathfrak{m}_S^n\subseteq\mathfrak{m}_R S$, a power bound by induction, iterative approximation, then Nakayama. The key step approximates elements of $\mathfrak{q}$ by $R[\beta]$ modulo $(\pi^n)+\mathfrak{m}_R S$.

nodes.name: Adjustment by principal generator
nodes.statement: Let $(R, \mathfrak{m}_R)$ and $(S, \mathfrak{m}_S)$ be local domains with $R$ integrally closed and $S$ a finite $R$-algebra with faithful scalar action. Let $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ be a prime ideal with $\mathfrak{q} = (q_0)$, and let $\beta \in S$, $f_1 \in R[X]$, $a \in S$ satisfy: \begin{enumerate} \item $f_1(\beta) = q_0 \cdot a$ with $a \in \mathfrak{m}_S$, \item $f_1'(\beta) \notin \mathfrak{m}_S$, \item $\mathfrak{m}_S = \mathfrak{q} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$, \item $\bar\beta$ generates $S/\mathfrak{q}$ over $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R)$. \end{enumerate} Then there exist a monic $f \in R[X]$ and an $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure for $S$ over $f$.
assumptions: Let $(R, \mathfrak{m}_R)$ and $(S, \mathfrak{m}_S)$ be local domains with $R$ integrally closed and $S$ a finite $R$-algebra with faithful scalar action.
Let $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ be a prime ideal with $\mathfrak{q} = (q_0)$,
$f_1(\beta) = q_0 \cdot a$ with $a \in \mathfrak{m}_S$,
$f_1'(\beta) \notin \mathfrak{m}_S$,
$\mathfrak{m}_S = \mathfrak{q} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$,
$\bar\beta$ generates $S/\mathfrak{q}$ over $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R)$.
conclusions: Then there exist a monic $f \in R[X]$ and an $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure for $S$ over $f$.
nodes.statement_short: Under the stated conditions on $\beta, f_1, a$, replacing $\beta$ by $\beta+q_0$ makes $S$ monogenic over $R$.
nodes.label: lem:exists_isAdjoinRootMonic_of_principal_adjust

nodes.name: Proof of the principal adjustment lemma
nodes.statement: Set $\beta' = \beta + q_0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:taylor_expansion}, $f_1(\beta') = q_0 \cdot (a + f_1'(\beta) + q_0 b)$ for some $b \in S$. Since $f_1'(\beta) \notin \mathfrak{m}_S$ and $a, q_0 b \in \mathfrak{m}_S$ (the former by hypothesis), the cofactor is a unit. Hence $\operatorname{span}\{f_1(\beta')\} = \mathfrak{q}$, and $\mathfrak{m}_S = \operatorname{span}\{f_1(\beta')\} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$. Since $\beta' \equiv \beta \pmod{\mathfrak{q}}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:quotient_adjust}), it still generates the quotient, so Lemma~\ref{lem:adjoin_eq_top_of_quotient} gives $R[\beta'] = S$. Finally, Theorem~\ref{thm:mkOfAdjoinEqTop} provides the $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure for $\operatorname{minpoly}_R \beta'$.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor-expand $f_1$ at $\beta'=\beta+q_0$ so $f_1(\beta')$ generates $\mathfrak{q}$, then the Nakayama lemma and the quotient isomorphism.

nodes.name: Monogenicity from étale height-one quotient
nodes.statement: Let $(R, \mathfrak{m}_R)$ and $(S, \mathfrak{m}_S)$ be local domains with $R$ integrally closed and $S$ a UFD. Let $R \to S$ be a finite injective ring homomorphism. If there exists a prime ideal $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ of height~1 such that the induced map $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R) \to S/\mathfrak{q}$ is étale, then there exist a monic $f \in R[X]$ and an $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure for $S$ over $f$.
assumptions: Let $(R, \mathfrak{m}_R)$ and $(S, \mathfrak{m}_S)$ be local domains with $R$ integrally closed and $S$ a UFD.
Let $R \to S$ be a finite injective ring homomorphism.
there exists a prime ideal $\mathfrak{q} \subset S$ of height~1 such that the induced map $R/(\mathfrak{q} \cap R) \to S/\mathfrak{q}$ is étale,
conclusions: there exist a monic $f \in R[X]$ and an $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure for $S$ over $f$.
also_stated_at: If a finite map of local rings admits an étale quotient through a height-one prime, the extension is monogenic.
nodes.statement_short: A finite extension of local domains ($R$ integrally closed, $S$ a UFD) with an étale quotient through a height-one prime is monogenic.
nodes.label: thm:exists_isAdjoinRootMonic_of_quotientMap_etale

nodes.name: Proof of monogenicity from étale height-one quotient
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 1: $R \to S$ is already étale.} Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:exists_adjoin_eq_top} to find $\beta$ with $R[\beta] = S$, then Theorem~\ref{thm:mkOfAdjoinEqTop} for the isomorphism. \textbf{Case 2: $R \to S$ is not étale.} Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:exists_adjoin_eq_top} to the étale quotient $R_0 = R/\mathfrak{p} \to S_0 = S/\mathfrak{q}$ to get $\beta_0 \in S_0$ with $R_0[\beta_0] = S_0$. Lift to $\beta \in S$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:height_one_principal}, $\mathfrak{q} = (q_0)$ for some $q_0 \in S$. Lift the minimal polynomial $f_0 = \operatorname{minpoly}_{R_0} \beta_0$ to a monic $f_1 \in R[X]$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:maximalIdeal_eq_sup}, $\mathfrak{m}_S = \mathfrak{q} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$. \textbf{Sub-case 2a:} If $f_1(\beta)$ generates $\mathfrak{m}_S$ modulo $\mathfrak{m}_R S$, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:adjoin_eq_top_of_quotient} directly to conclude $R[\beta] = S$. \textbf{Sub-case 2b:} Otherwise, since $f_1(\beta) \in \mathfrak{q} = (q_0)$, write $f_1(\beta) = q_0 \cdot a$. If $a$ were a unit, then $\operatorname{span}\{f_1(\beta)\} = \mathfrak{q}$ and Sub-case~2a would apply; so $a \in \mathfrak{m}_S$. The derivative condition $f_1'(\beta) \notin \mathfrak{m}_S$ follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:isUnit_aeval_derivative_minpoly} applied to the étale quotient. Now apply Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_isAdjoinRootMonic_of_principal_adjust} with $q_0$, $\beta$, $f_1$, and $a$.
nodes.statement_short: Case split on whether $R\to S$ is étale; otherwise lift a generator from the étale quotient and either apply the Nakayama lemma or the principal adjustment lemma.

nodes.name: Proof structure of Lemma 3.1 (PR plan)
nodes.statement: Case split on whether $R \to S$ is already étale. Case 1 uses PR~3 + PR~1 directly. Case 2 lifts a generator from the étale quotient, then either (2a) applies the Nakayama argument directly, or (2b) extracts $a$ with $f_1(\beta) = q_0 \cdot a$ and shows $a \in \mathfrak{m}_S$ (if $a$ were a unit, Sub-case~2a would apply), then delegates to \texttt{exists\_isAdjoinRootMonic\_of\_principal\_adjust}. \textbf{Notes:} \begin{itemize} \item The hypotheses include \texttt{IsIntegrallyClosed R} and \texttt{UniqueFactorizationMonoid S}. These are strong; reviewers may ask whether they can be weakened. \item An alternative formulation with an explicit ring homomorphism (transferring between $\operatorname{Algebra.adjoin}\;R$ and $\operatorname{Algebra.adjoin}\;\varphi(R)$) could be added as a trivial corollary if needed. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: case split on étaleness; Case 2 lifts a quotient generator then uses the Nakayama argument or the principal adjustment.

nodes.name: Cayley-Hamilton
nodes.statement: Let $\ell_\alpha = \operatorname{Algebra.lmul}_R\, \alpha$ be the left-multiplication endomorphism. By Cayley--Hamilton ($\mathtt{LinearMap.aeval\_self\_charpoly}$), $\operatorname{aeval}_\alpha(\operatorname{charpoly}(\ell_\alpha)) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Cayley-Hamilton to the multiplication map $\ell_\alpha$

nodes.name: Divisibility gives bound
nodes.statement: Since $\operatorname{charpoly}(\ell_\alpha)$ is monic, the minimal polynomial divides it, so $\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_R \alpha) \le \deg(\operatorname{charpoly}(\ell_\alpha)) = \operatorname{finrank}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: Minpoly divides the monic charpoly; compare degrees

nodes.name: Well-defined and surjective
nodes.statement: The map $\varphi$ is well-defined since $f(\alpha) = 0$, and surjective since $R[\alpha] = S$.
nodes.statement_short: $\varphi$ is well-defined and surjective

nodes.name: Rank equality
nodes.statement: \textbf{Rank equality.} The upper bound $\deg f \le \operatorname{finrank}_R S$ follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:minpoly_natDegree_le}. For the lower bound, consider the surjection $\varphi$. By the quotient rank formula ($\mathtt{finrank\_quotient\_}\allowbreak\mathtt{span\_eq\_natDegree'}$), $\operatorname{finrank}_R(R[X]/(f)) = \deg f$. Since $\varphi$ is surjective, $\operatorname{finrank}_R S \le \operatorname{finrank}_R(R[X]/(f)) = \deg f$. Hence $\deg f = \operatorname{finrank}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\deg f = \operatorname{finrank}_R S$

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement: \textbf{Rank equality.} The upper bound $\deg f \le \operatorname{finrank}_R S$ follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:minpoly_natDegree_le}.
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound from the degree bound lemma

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement: For the lower bound, consider the surjection $\varphi$. By the quotient rank formula ($\mathtt{finrank\_quotient\_}\allowbreak\mathtt{span\_eq\_natDegree'}$), $\operatorname{finrank}_R(R[X]/(f)) = \deg f$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound from the quotient rank formula and surjectivity

nodes.name: Equality
nodes.statement: Hence $\deg f = \operatorname{finrank}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the bounds

nodes.name: Injectivity
nodes.statement: \textbf{Injectivity.} Since both $R[X]/(f)$ and $S$ are free $R$-modules of the same finite rank, and $\varphi$ is surjective, the composite $e^{-1} \circ \varphi$ is a surjective endomorphism of a finitely generated free module (where $e$ is a linear equivalence from the rank equality). By $\mathtt{OrzechProperty.}\allowbreak\mathtt{injective\_of\_surjective\_endomorphism}$ (which holds for all commutative rings), this composite is injective, hence $\varphi$ is injective.
nodes.statement_short: Surjective endomorphism of a f.g. free module is injective (Orzech)

nodes.name: Étale implies free
nodes.statement: Since $R \to S$ is étale, it is smooth, hence flat. Finite + flat over a local ring implies free ($\mathtt{Module.free\_of\_flat\_of\_isLocalRing}$).
nodes.statement_short: Étale gives smooth, flat, hence free

nodes.name: Maximal ideal extends
nodes.statement: The étale condition gives $\mathfrak{m}_R \cdot S = \mathfrak{m}_S$ ($\mathtt{Algebra.FormallyUnramified.}\allowbreak\mathtt{map\_maximalIdeal}$), so $S / \mathfrak{m}_R S \cong k_S$.
nodes.statement_short: Unramifiedness gives $\mathfrak{m}_R S=\mathfrak{m}_S$

nodes.name: Rank of quotient
nodes.statement: By $\mathtt{IsLocalRing.finrank\_quotient\_map}$, $\operatorname{finrank}_{k_R}(S/\mathfrak{m}_R S) = \operatorname{finrank}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: Rank of $S/\mathfrak{m}_R S$ over $k_R$ equals rank of $S$

nodes.name: Transfer rank
nodes.statement: The quotient equivalence from $\mathfrak{m}_R S = \mathfrak{m}_S$ transfers the finrank.
nodes.statement_short: Transfer the rank via the quotient equivalence

nodes.name: Divisibility
nodes.statement: Set $f = \operatorname{minpoly}_R \beta$, $\bar f = f \bmod \mathfrak{m}_R$, $g = \operatorname{minpoly}_{k_R} \bar\beta$. Since $\bar\beta$ is a root of $\bar f$ (by $\mathtt{hom\_eval_2}$), we have $g \mid \bar f$. Both $f$ and $g$ are monic, and $\bar f$ is monic.
nodes.section: 3.3 Minimal Polynomial Descends to Residue Field
nodes.statement_short: Set notation; $g$ divides $\bar f$; all monic

nodes.name: Degree chain
nodes.statement: The degree chain: \begin{align*} \deg \bar f &= \deg f && \text{(monic polynomial preserves degree under reduction)} \\ &= \operatorname{finrank}_R S && \text{(Theorem~\ref{thm:mkOfAdjoinEqTop})} \\ &= \operatorname{finrank}_{k_R} k_S && \text{(Lemma~\ref{lem:finrank_eq_finrank_residueField})} \\ &= [k_R(\bar\beta) : k_R] && \text{(Lemma~\ref{lem:adjoin_residue_eq_top}: } k_R[\bar\beta] = k_S \text{)} \\ &= \deg g && \text{(degree of minimal polynomial = extension degree)} \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3.3 Minimal Polynomial Descends to Residue Field
nodes.statement_short: Chain of degree equalities via Theorem 1 and Lemmas 2-3

nodes.name: Equality
nodes.statement: Since $g \mid \bar f$, both are monic, and they have the same degree, $\bar f = g$.
nodes.section: 3.3 Minimal Polynomial Descends to Residue Field
nodes.statement_short: Monic, divisible, equal degree gives equality

nodes.name: Reduce to residue
nodes.statement: Since $S$ is a local ring, it suffices to show $\overline{f'(\beta)} \ne 0$ in $k_S$ ($\mathtt{IsLocalRing.}\allowbreak\mathtt{residue\_ne\_zero\_iff\_isUnit}$).
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to show the residue is nonzero

nodes.name: Separability
nodes.statement: Since $R \to S$ is étale, the residue field extension $k_R \to k_S$ is separable. By Lemma~\ref{lem:minpoly_map_residue}, $\bar f = \operatorname{minpoly}_{k_R} \bar\beta$, so $\bar f$ is separable ($\mathtt{Algebra.IsSeparable.isSeparable}$).
nodes.statement_short: Residue minimal polynomial is separable

nodes.name: Nonvanishing derivative
nodes.statement: This means $\bar{f'}(\bar\beta) \ne 0$ ($\mathtt{Separable.aeval\_derivative\_ne\_zero}$).
nodes.statement_short: Separable gives nonzero derivative at $\bar\beta$

nodes.name: Lift back
nodes.statement: By $\mathtt{hom\_eval_2}$, $\overline{f'(\beta)} = \bar{f'}(\bar\beta) \ne 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Residue of $f'(\beta)$ is nonzero

nodes.name: Lift primitive element
nodes.statement: By the primitive element theorem ($\mathtt{Field.exists\_primitive\_element}$), there exists $\beta_0 \in k_S$ with $k_R[\beta_0] = k_S$. Lift $\beta_0$ to $\beta \in S$ via $\mathtt{Ideal.Quotient.mk\_surjective}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lift a primitive element of $k_S/k_R$

nodes.name: Nakayama reduction
nodes.statement: It suffices to show $\operatorname{Algebra.adjoin} R \{\beta\} = \top$. By Nakayama's lemma ($\mathtt{Submodule.}\allowbreak\mathtt{le\_of\_le\_smul\_of\_le\_jacobson\_bot}$), it suffices to show $S \subseteq R[\beta] + \mathfrak{m}_R \cdot S$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $S\subseteq R[\beta]+\mathfrak{m}_R S$

nodes.name: Approximate
nodes.statement: For any $s \in S$, the residue $\bar s \in k_S = k_R[\beta_0]$, so there exists $t_0 \in R[\beta]$ with $\overline{t_0} = \bar s$. Then $s - t_0 \in \mathfrak{m}_S = \mathfrak{m}_R \cdot S$ (using the étale condition $\mathtt{Algebra.FormallyUnramified.map\_maximalIdeal}$).
nodes.statement_short: Approximate each $s$ modulo $\mathfrak{m}_S=\mathfrak{m}_R S$

nodes.name: Standard étale pair
nodes.statement: Construct a $\mathtt{StandardEtalePair}$ using $(f, f')$: the Bézout relation $f' \cdot 1 + f \cdot 0 = (f')^1$ is trivially satisfied. The natural map $P.\mathtt{lift} \colon P.\mathtt{Ring} \to S$ sending $X \mapsto \beta$ is well-defined by $f(\beta) = 0$ and the unit condition on $f'(\beta)$.
nodes.section: 4 Converse: Monogenic with Unit Derivative Implies \'Etale
nodes.statement_short: Build the standard étale pair $(f,f')$ and its well-defined lift to $S$

nodes.name: Explicit inverse
nodes.statement: Construct an explicit inverse via $\mathtt{AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom}$ composed with the algebra equivalence $S \cong \mathtt{AdjoinRoot}\; f$. Verify it is both a left and right inverse by checking on generators, concluding bijectivity.
nodes.section: 4 Converse: Monogenic with Unit Derivative Implies \'Etale
nodes.statement_short: Inverse via AdjoinRoot.liftAlgHom; check on generators

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence $S$ is standard étale ($\mathtt{Algebra.IsStandardEtale}$), and étale follows.
nodes.section: 4 Converse: Monogenic with Unit Derivative Implies \'Etale
nodes.statement_short: Standard étale implies étale

nodes.name: Irreducible element
nodes.statement: Since $\mathfrak{q} \ne 0$, it contains an irreducible element $p$. Then $\operatorname{span}\{p\}$ is prime and contained in $\mathfrak{q}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick irreducible $p$; $(p)$ is a prime in $\mathfrak{q}$

nodes.name: Height contradiction
nodes.statement: If $\operatorname{span}\{p\} \subsetneq \mathfrak{q}$, then $\operatorname{height}(\operatorname{span}\{p\}) < \operatorname{height}(\mathfrak{q}) = 1$, forcing $\operatorname{span}\{p\} = 0$, contradicting $p \ne 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Proper inclusion would force height 0

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence $\mathfrak{q} = \operatorname{span}\{p\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak{q}=(p)$

nodes.name: Artinian bound
nodes.statement: Set $A = R[\beta]$. The quotient $S/\mathfrak{m}_R S$ is Artinian (finite over the field $k_R$), so $\mathfrak{m}_S^n \subseteq \mathfrak{m}_R S$ for some $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Artinian quotient gives $\mathfrak{m}_S^n\subseteq\mathfrak{m}_R S$

nodes.name: Power bound
nodes.statement: \textbf{Power bound.} By induction, $\mathfrak{m}_S^k \subseteq \operatorname{span}\{\pi^k\} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$, using the hypothesis on $\mathfrak{m}_S$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction: $\mathfrak{m}_S^k\subseteq(\pi^k)+\mathfrak{m}_R S$

nodes.name: Iterative reduction
nodes.statement: \textbf{Iterative reduction.} For $x \in \mathfrak{q}$, by repeated application of quotient lifting (Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_adjoin_sub_mem}) and the power bound, we find $a \in A$ with $x - a \in \operatorname{span}\{\pi^n\} + \mathfrak{m}_R S \subseteq \mathfrak{m}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $x\in\mathfrak{q}$ by $A$ via repeated quotient lifting

nodes.name: Nakayama
nodes.statement: Hence $\mathfrak{q} \subseteq A + \mathfrak{m}_R S$ as $R$-submodules. Combined with the quotient lifting for general elements, $S \subseteq A + \mathfrak{m}_R S$. By Nakayama's lemma, $A = S$.
nodes.statement_short: Get $S\subseteq A+\mathfrak{m}_R S$ and apply Nakayama

nodes.name: Taylor expansion
nodes.statement: Set $\beta' = \beta + q_0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:taylor_expansion}, $f_1(\beta') = q_0 \cdot (a + f_1'(\beta) + q_0 b)$ for some $b \in S$.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor-expand $f_1$ at $\beta'=\beta+q_0$

nodes.name: Unit cofactor
nodes.statement: Since $f_1'(\beta) \notin \mathfrak{m}_S$ and $a, q_0 b \in \mathfrak{m}_S$ (the former by hypothesis), the cofactor is a unit.
nodes.statement_short: The cofactor is a unit

nodes.name: Generator of q
nodes.statement: Hence $\operatorname{span}\{f_1(\beta')\} = \mathfrak{q}$, and $\mathfrak{m}_S = \operatorname{span}\{f_1(\beta')\} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: $f_1(\beta')$ generates $\mathfrak{q}$

nodes.name: Nakayama
nodes.statement: Since $\beta' \equiv \beta \pmod{\mathfrak{q}}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:quotient_adjust}), it still generates the quotient, so Lemma~\ref{lem:adjoin_eq_top_of_quotient} gives $R[\beta'] = S$.
nodes.statement_short: $\beta'$ still generates the quotient; apply Lemma 10

nodes.name: Isomorphism
nodes.statement: Finally, Theorem~\ref{thm:mkOfAdjoinEqTop} provides the $\mathtt{IsAdjoinRootMonic}$ structure for $\operatorname{minpoly}_R \beta'$.
nodes.statement_short: Quotient isomorphism gives the structure

nodes.name: Case 1: étale
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 1: $R \to S$ is already étale.} Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:exists_adjoin_eq_top} to find $\beta$ with $R[\beta] = S$, then Theorem~\ref{thm:mkOfAdjoinEqTop} for the isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Étale case: generator exists, then quotient isomorphism

nodes.name: Case 2: not étale
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 2: $R \to S$ is not étale.} Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:exists_adjoin_eq_top} to the étale quotient $R_0 = R/\mathfrak{p} \to S_0 = S/\mathfrak{q}$ to get $\beta_0 \in S_0$ with $R_0[\beta_0] = S_0$. Lift to $\beta \in S$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:height_one_principal}, $\mathfrak{q} = (q_0)$ for some $q_0 \in S$. Lift the minimal polynomial $f_0 = \operatorname{minpoly}_{R_0} \beta_0$ to a monic $f_1 \in R[X]$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:maximalIdeal_eq_sup}, $\mathfrak{m}_S = \mathfrak{q} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$. \textbf{Sub-case 2a:} If $f_1(\beta)$ generates $\mathfrak{m}_S$ modulo $\mathfrak{m}_R S$, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:adjoin_eq_top_of_quotient} directly to conclude $R[\beta] = S$. \textbf{Sub-case 2b:} Otherwise, since $f_1(\beta) \in \mathfrak{q} = (q_0)$, write $f_1(\beta) = q_0 \cdot a$. If $a$ were a unit, then $\operatorname{span}\{f_1(\beta)\} = \mathfrak{q}$ and Sub-case~2a would apply; so $a \in \mathfrak{m}_S$. The derivative condition $f_1'(\beta) \notin \mathfrak{m}_S$ follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:isUnit_aeval_derivative_minpoly} applied to the étale quotient. Now apply Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_isAdjoinRootMonic_of_principal_adjust} with $q_0$, $\beta$, $f_1$, and $a$.
nodes.statement_short: Non-étale case via the étale quotient

nodes.name: Lift quotient generator
nodes.statement: \textbf{Case 2: $R \to S$ is not étale.} Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:exists_adjoin_eq_top} to the étale quotient $R_0 = R/\mathfrak{p} \to S_0 = S/\mathfrak{q}$ to get $\beta_0 \in S_0$ with $R_0[\beta_0] = S_0$. Lift to $\beta \in S$.
nodes.statement_short: Generator of the étale quotient, lifted to $S$

nodes.name: Principal prime and lift
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:height_one_principal}, $\mathfrak{q} = (q_0)$ for some $q_0 \in S$. Lift the minimal polynomial $f_0 = \operatorname{minpoly}_{R_0} \beta_0$ to a monic $f_1 \in R[X]$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak{q}=(q_0)$; lift minpoly to monic $f_1$

nodes.name: Maximal ideal decomposition
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:maximalIdeal_eq_sup}, $\mathfrak{m}_S = \mathfrak{q} + \mathfrak{m}_R S$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak{m}_S=\mathfrak{q}+\mathfrak{m}_R S$

nodes.name: Sub-case 2a
nodes.statement: \textbf{Sub-case 2a:} If $f_1(\beta)$ generates $\mathfrak{m}_S$ modulo $\mathfrak{m}_R S$, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:adjoin_eq_top_of_quotient} directly to conclude $R[\beta] = S$.
nodes.statement_short: If $f_1(\beta)$ generates, apply Lemma 10 directly

nodes.name: Sub-case 2b
nodes.statement: \textbf{Sub-case 2b:} Otherwise, since $f_1(\beta) \in \mathfrak{q} = (q_0)$, write $f_1(\beta) = q_0 \cdot a$. If $a$ were a unit, then $\operatorname{span}\{f_1(\beta)\} = \mathfrak{q}$ and Sub-case~2a would apply; so $a \in \mathfrak{m}_S$. The derivative condition $f_1'(\beta) \notin \mathfrak{m}_S$ follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:isUnit_aeval_derivative_minpoly} applied to the étale quotient. Now apply Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_isAdjoinRootMonic_of_principal_adjust} with $q_0$, $\beta$, $f_1$, and $a$.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise use the principal adjustment lemma

nodes.name: a in maximal ideal
nodes.statement: \textbf{Sub-case 2b:} Otherwise, since $f_1(\beta) \in \mathfrak{q} = (q_0)$, write $f_1(\beta) = q_0 \cdot a$. If $a$ were a unit, then $\operatorname{span}\{f_1(\beta)\} = \mathfrak{q}$ and Sub-case~2a would apply; so $a \in \mathfrak{m}_S$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $f_1(\beta)=q_0a$; $a$ is not a unit

nodes.name: Derivative condition
nodes.statement: The derivative condition $f_1'(\beta) \notin \mathfrak{m}_S$ follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:isUnit_aeval_derivative_minpoly} applied to the étale quotient.
nodes.statement_short: Unit derivative from Theorem 2 on the quotient

nodes.name: Apply adjustment
nodes.statement: Now apply Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_isAdjoinRootMonic_of_principal_adjust} with $q_0$, $\beta$, $f_1$, and $a$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 11

nodes.name: Proof structure
nodes.statement: Case split on whether $R \to S$ is already étale. Case 1 uses PR~3 + PR~1 directly. Case 2 lifts a generator from the étale quotient, then either (2a) applies the Nakayama argument directly, or (2b) extracts $a$ with $f_1(\beta) = q_0 \cdot a$ and shows $a \in \mathfrak{m}_S$ (if $a$ were a unit, Sub-case~2a would apply), then delegates to \texttt{exists\_isAdjoinRootMonic\_of\_principal\_adjust}.
nodes.statement_short: Case split and delegation to sub-lemmas

nodes.name: Notes
nodes.statement: \textbf{Notes:} \begin{itemize} \item The hypotheses include \texttt{IsIntegrallyClosed R} and \texttt{UniqueFactorizationMonoid S}. These are strong; reviewers may ask whether they can be weakened. \item An alternative formulation with an explicit ring homomorphism (transferring between $\operatorname{Algebra.adjoin}\;R$ and $\operatorname{Algebra.adjoin}\;\varphi(R)$) could be added as a trivial corollary if needed. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Remarks on hypotheses and alternative formulations

nodes.name: Strong hypotheses
nodes.statement: The hypotheses include \texttt{IsIntegrallyClosed R} and \texttt{UniqueFactorizationMonoid S}. These are strong; reviewers may ask whether they can be weakened.
nodes.statement_short: Hypotheses may be weakenable

nodes.name: Alternative formulation
nodes.statement: An alternative formulation with an explicit ring homomorphism (transferring between $\operatorname{Algebra.adjoin}\;R$ and $\operatorname{Algebra.adjoin}\;\varphi(R)$) could be added as a trivial corollary if needed.
nodes.statement_short: Possible corollary with explicit ring hom
